ai.literal: Reality things that are not reality saying perceiving by delusion becomes inglorious birth.
ai.translation: Wretched birth comes from the delusion of perceiving things that are unreal as reality.
ai.modern: உண்மையான பொருள் அல்லாதவைகளை உண்மையான பொருள் என்று தவறாக உணரும் மயக்கத்தால், சிறப்பற்ற பிறப்பு உண்டாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the root cause of the cycle of birth and suffering. It states that taking unreal or impermanent things to be the ultimate reality is a delusion. From this fundamental misunderstanding arises a wretched, endless cycle of birth. The word porul here denotes true substance or ultimate reality, contrasting with the illusion of worldly attachments.

ai.literal: Darkness having departed, joy it will yield; delusion having departed, blemish-severed vision to them.
ai.translation: For those of flawless vision who have freed themselves from delusion, the darkness of ignorance will depart and yield lasting joy.
ai.modern: மயக்கம் நீங்கி குற்றமற்ற மெய்யறிவைப் பெற்றவர்களுக்கு, அறியாமை இருள் விலகி இன்பம் உண்டாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the reward of attaining true understanding. The word 'மருள்' refers to the delusion or confusion that clouds the mind, while 'மாசறு காட்சி' denotes a clear, flawless vision of reality. When a person achieves this state, the 'இருள்' or darkness of ignorance and suffering vanishes. In its place, this clarity of vision yields profound and lasting joy ('இன்பம் பயக்கும்').

ai.literal: From doubt having departed to those who are clear, than the earth heaven nearness possesses.
ai.translation: To those who have freed themselves from doubt and attained clarity, heaven is nearer than the earth.
ai.modern: ஐயங்களிலிருந்து விடுபட்டு தெளிந்த அறிவைப் பெற்றவர்களுக்கு, இந்த உலகத்தை விட வானுலகம் மிகவும் நெருக்கமானதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the power of clear, doubt-free understanding. The phrase 'ஐயத்தின் நீங்கி' means departing from all uncertainties and illusions. For those who achieve such flawless clarity ('தெளிந்தார்க்கு'), the ultimate state of heaven ('வானம்') becomes closer and more accessible than the physical earth ('வையத்தின்') they stand on. The word 'நணியது' denotes nearness, showing that spiritual liberation is immediately within reach for the truly realized.

ai.literal: Five senses attained even when, benefit is not indeed, truth knowledge to those who lack.
ai.translation: Even if one has attained mastery over the five senses, there is no benefit to those who lack the realization of truth.
ai.modern: ஐம்புலன்களையும் அடக்கியாளும் திறனை அடைந்திருந்தாலும், உண்மையை உணரும் அறிவு இல்லாதவர்களுக்கு அதனால் எந்தப் பயனும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: The couplet contrasts the mastery of the physical senses with the realization of ultimate truth. The phrase 'ஐயுணர்வு' refers to the perception or mastery of the five senses, while 'மெய்யுணர்வு' denotes the knowledge of true reality. The text states that even if a person has successfully attained control over their five senses, this achievement yields no real benefit if they still lack the understanding of truth. Thus, sensory discipline is shown to be incomplete without the deeper realization of reality.

ai.literal: Whatever thing, of whatever nature even if it is, of that thing the true substance seeing is wisdom.
ai.translation: Whatever the thing may be and whatever its nature, wisdom is seeing the true substance of that thing.
ai.modern: எந்தப் பொருள் எந்தத் தன்மையைக் கொண்டிருந்தாலும், அந்தப் பொருளின் உண்மையான தன்மையைக் காண்பதே மெய்யறிவாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines true wisdom as the ability to see past the surface of things. The phrase 'epporul ettanmaittu ayinum' acknowledges that things in the world present themselves in countless forms and appearances. However, 'meypporul' refers to the underlying truth or reality of those things. True knowledge, therefore, is not distracted by outward characteristics but penetrates to the core reality of whatever it encounters.

ai.literal: Having learned, here true reality those who saw, will attain again here not-coming path.
ai.translation: Those who have learned and realized the true reality in this world will attain the path that does not lead back here again.
ai.modern: கற்க வேண்டியவற்றைக் கற்று, இவ்வுலகில் உண்மையான பொருளைக் கண்டவர்கள், மீண்டும் இவ்வுலகிற்குப் பிறந்து வராத வழியை அடைவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the ultimate reward for realizing the truth. The word 'ஈண்டு' can mean 'abundantly' or 'here', but 'here' best fits the context of worldly existence. By learning deeply and seeing the true reality (மெய்ப்பொருள்) while living here, a person achieves the highest goal. They will enter the path (நெறி) that ensures they do not return here again (மற்று ஈண்டு வாரா), signifying freedom from returning to this worldly life.

ai.literal: Having pondered, mind, that which is, if realizes, certainly, again, to think of, is not needed, birth.
ai.translation: If the mind ponders and realizes the ultimate truth, there will certainly be no need to think of birth again.
ai.modern: உள்ளமானது ஆராய்ந்து உண்மையான பொருளை உணர்ந்தால், மீண்டும் பிறவி எடுப்பதைப் பற்றி நினைக்க வேண்டியதில்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the result of realizing the ultimate truth. The word 'ஓர்த்து' means to examine or ponder deeply, while 'உள்ளது' refers to that which truly exists, or reality. If the mind grasps this reality, the cycle of birth is broken. Therefore, one will 'certainly' ('ஒருதலையா') not need to worry about or experience another birth ('பேர்த்து உள்ள வேண்டா பிறப்பு'). The verse emphasizes that true understanding frees the mind from the cycle of worldly existence.

ai.explanation: This couplet defines true knowledge as the realization of ultimate reality. It contrasts the cycle of birth, which it equates with ignorance, against the supreme excellence of truth. By perceiving this perfect truth, the delusion that causes rebirth is dispelled. The word செம்பொருள் refers to the flawless, ultimate reality that stands in opposition to the transient nature of worldly existence.

ai.translation: If one realizes the true support and lives so that worldly attachments perish, the sufferings that usually approach will not come to destroy one again.
ai.modern: உண்மையான சார்பினை உணர்ந்து, உலகப் பற்றுக்கள் அழியுமாறு வாழ்ந்தால், இயல்பாக வந்து சேரும் துன்பங்கள் மீண்டும் வந்து அழித்துச் சேராது.
ai.explanation: The word 'cārpu' is used twice with two different meanings: first as the ultimate truth or true support, and second as worldly attachments. The sufferings ('nōy') that naturally approach all beings will not return to destroy such a person again.

ai.literal: Desire, anger, delusion - of these three, [when] name perishes, perishes disease.
ai.translation: When even the names of these three—desire, anger, and delusion—are destroyed, the disease of suffering will also perish.
ai.modern: காமம், சினம், மயக்கம் ஆகிய இந்த மூன்றின் பெயரும் கூட இல்லாமல் அழிந்தால், ஒருவருக்கு வரும் துன்பமும் அழியும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet identifies three root causes of human suffering: desire, anger, and delusion. It states that true perception involves eradicating these flaws so completely that even their 'name' (நாமம்) ceases to exist within the mind. When these three are entirely destroyed, the 'disease' (நோய்) of suffering that they cause will also perish. The metaphor of disease emphasizes that suffering is an affliction which can only be cured by removing its underlying causes.
